org.title: Grants to Enhance Access to Environmental Justice in Türkiye
org.who: National and local civil society organisations registered and operating in Türkiye.
req: Application in English
Registration certificate and statute of the CSO
Proof of bank account and recent financial records
Project for people and communities affected by pollution, environmental damage or climate-related harm
org.how: Email the full application to the Council of Europe Programme Office in Ankara before the deadline (see call documents).
org.tip: Strong fit for IDDA's climate work: combine environmental education with information and legal-awareness activities for affected communities.

org.title: Grants to Enhance Access to Justice in the Context of Migration
org.amount: Up to 10 grants (see call for ceilings)
org.who: Civil society organisations legally constituted and operating in Türkiye.
req: Projects improving access to justice, legal and other services for people in the context of migration
Application package sent by email with the reference CSF/GRANTS/CSO/Migration
Results expected around 15 January 2027
org.how: Send the application by email to the CoE Ankara office before 30 November 2026, 16:00 Türkiye time.
org.tip: Relevant if IDDA partners with a legal-aid or refugee-support organisation; IDDA can contribute digital tools and training.

org.title: Prosperous Future Grant Programme (Nordic–Baltic civil society cooperation)
org.who: Civil society organisations from the Nordic countries, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania and Poland (plus Ukraine-related actors and democratic Belarusian and Russian partners). Türkiye is not eligible.
req: Cooperation between at least 3 eligible countries
Contribute to a green, competitive and socially sustainable Nordic–Baltic region
Mainstream environment & climate, gender equality, and child-rights & youth perspectives
org.how: Apply online at ncmprosperousfuturegrants.org.
org.tip: Apply through IDDA's Estonian organisation with one Nordic and one Baltic partner; youth climate or digital-resilience projects fit well.

org.title: CERV: EU Values & European Remembrance calls
org.funder: European Commission (CERV programme) · national contact point KÜSK
org.amount: EU co-funding up to 90% of the project budget
org.who: Non-profit organisations established in EU member states (CERV is not open to Türkiye-based applicants).
req: Projects on democracy, EU values, civic participation or European historical memory
Usually transnational partnerships
Submitted on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal
org.how: Prepare via the EU Funding & Tenders Portal; KÜSK (Estonia's CERV contact point) offers guidance.
org.tip: Pairs well with IDDA's civic-engagement pillar; please confirm the exact deadline on the Funding & Tenders Portal before you plan.

org.title: Erasmus+ Cooperation Partnerships (KA220)
org.funder: European Union · Türkiye National Agency / HARNO (Estonia)
org.who: Any organisation in an Erasmus+ programme country (incl. Türkiye and Estonia): NGOs, schools, universities, municipalities, companies.
req: At least 3 organisations from 3 different programme countries
12–36 months, results with European added value
Fields: youth, school, adult education, VET or higher education
org.how: Submit through your National Agency (Türkiye Ulusal Ajansı or HARNO in Estonia). Check your National Agency for the exact submission time.
org.tip: IDDA's core instrument (like Solar4Future+). Start partner search and concept now; aim to finalise by mid-February.

org.title: Erasmus+ Small-scale Partnerships (KA210)
org.dlText: Expected March 2027 (round 1) and October 2027 (round 2)
org.who: Organisations in Erasmus+ programme countries; designed for newcomers and smaller organisations.
req: At least 2 organisations from 2 programme countries
6–24 months
Simple application, ideal for first-time coordinators
org.how: Apply via your National Agency. Confirm dates in the 2027 Erasmus+ Programme Guide.
org.tip: Good entry point for new partners or pilot ideas before scaling up to KA220.

org.title: Erasmus+ Youth Exchanges, Youth Worker Mobility & Youth Participation (KA152 / KA153 / KA154)
org.dlText: Next round expected February 2027 (2026 rounds were 12 February and 1 October)
org.amount: Unit-cost grants for travel, stay, organisation and inclusion support
org.who: Youth NGOs, informal groups of young people and other organisations in programme countries.
req: Youth exchanges for ages 13–30
Mobility for youth workers (training courses, job-shadowing)
Youth participation projects (KA154) can be national
org.how: Apply via your National Agency. IDDA's partner network can host or send groups.
org.tip: Quickest way to involve IDDA volunteers; plan the February round now.

org.title: European Solidarity Corps: Volunteering & Solidarity Projects
org.dlText: 2027 call is open; first deadline expected February 2027 (2026: 18 February)
org.amount: Volunteering costs, pocket money, inclusion support; Solidarity Projects up to 12 months
org.who: Organisations with an ESC Quality Label (volunteering); groups of young people aged 18–30 (Solidarity Projects).
req: Quality Label required to host or send volunteers
Young people 18–30 (up to 35 for humanitarian aid)
Projects addressing inclusion, environment, digital or democratic participation
org.how: Apply via your National Agency; register young people on the European Youth Portal.
org.tip: Volunteers could support IDDA's climate and digital-education activities in Eskişehir.

org.title: Swedish Consulate General Istanbul: Project Grants
org.funder: Consulate General of Sweden in Istanbul
org.dlText: Annual call: concept notes were due 24 July 2026 for 2027 projects; next call expected mid-2027
org.amount: Budget requested in TRY (no fixed range published)
org.who: Registered CSOs, foundations, associations, think tanks, trade unions and universities in Türkiye. Individuals and companies are not eligible.
req: Priorities: democratic participation of young people; freedom of expression and media freedom; human rights and access to justice; combating gender-based violence; trade & development
Gender equality perspective and anti-corruption practice required
Concept note in English first, full proposal if shortlisted
org.how: Email the concept-note template to the Consulate when the call opens.
org.tip: A youth-participation project with digital tools fits the 'young people's democratic participation' priority.

org.title: Ministry of Youth and Sports: Youth Project Support Programmes
org.dlText: Calls published during the year (e.g. a 200 million TL addiction-prevention call for NGOs opened in May 2026)
org.amount: Varies by call
org.who: Associations, foundations and sports clubs working with young people in Türkiye.
req: Projects aligned with national youth policy areas (volunteering, participation, employment & entrepreneurship, environment & climate, science & technology, social inclusion)
Online application via the ministry's project system
org.how: Follow gsb.gov.tr and the ministry's project portal for new calls.
org.tip: Watch for calls on digital skills, climate and volunteering that match IDDA's pillars.

org.title: BEBKA Technical Support Programme (TR41: Bursa, Eskişehir, Bilecik)
org.dlText: Yearly programme; the 2026 programme was announced on 9 February 2026; 2027 expected in early 2027
org.amount: In-kind training and consultancy support
org.who: Public bodies, local authorities, NGOs and other non-profit institutions in the TR41 region.
req: Training or consultancy that builds institutional capacity
Contribution to regional development
org.how: Apply via BEBKA's website when the yearly programme is announced.
org.tip: Use it to fund expert training (e.g. EU project management, digital tools) for IDDA staff and volunteers.

org.title: EEA Civil Society Fund Estonia (EEA & Norway Grants 2021–2028)
org.funder: Iceland, Liechtenstein & Norway · operated by Open Estonia Foundation and the Network of Estonian Nonprofit Organizations
org.dlText: First strategic call (€50,001–€120,000) closed 28 September 2026; further calls expected
org.amount: Strategic grants €50,001 – €120,000; other calls to follow
org.who: Non-profit associations and foundations established in Estonia.
req: Democracy, rule of law, human rights and civic participation
Optional partners from Iceland, Liechtenstein or Norway (bilateral cooperation)
org.how: Follow the fund operators' websites for new calls.
org.tip: A long-term source for IDDA's Estonian organisation; prepare a strategy-based project idea in advance.

org.title: KÜSK International Cooperation Support (travel grants & co-funding of foreign projects)
org.dlText: Yearly; 2026 rounds closed 19 November 2026; next expected autumn 2027
org.amount: Travel grants and co-funding for international projects
org.who: Estonian civil society organisations.
req: Travel to international events or partner meetings
Self-contribution (co-funding) for EU-funded projects such as Erasmus+ or CERV
org.how: Apply via kysk.ee when the round opens.
org.tip: Useful to cover the required own contribution in EU projects led by IDDA's Estonian organisation.

org.title: KÜSK Community Fund & NGO Development Leap
org.dlText: Spring rounds; in 2026 they closed on 3 May (Community Fund) and 20 May (Development Leap)
org.amount: Varies by call
org.who: Estonian non-profit associations and foundations.
req: Community Fund: local community initiatives
Development Leap: strengthening the organisation's capacity and sustainability
org.how: Apply via kysk.ee; information sessions are held before each round.
org.tip: Development Leap can fund IDDA Estonia's strategy, communications or digital capacity.

org.title: Nordic–Baltic NGO Cooperation Support Programme
org.funder: Nordic Council of Ministers' Office in Lithuania
org.dlText: Yearly; 2026 round ran 9 February – 23 March 2026; 2027 round expected similar
org.amount: Network cooperation grants
org.who: NGOs in the Baltic States cooperating with Nordic partners.
req: Network cooperation and knowledge exchange with Nordic organisations
Priorities aligned with the Nordic Council of Ministers' Vision 2030 (resilience, green, social)
org.how: Apply online via norden.lt during the call window.
org.tip: Smaller step before the Prosperous Future programme; good for building Nordic partnerships.

org.title: Grants for CSOs to Strengthen Women's Access to Justice
org.amount: Up to 10 grants (see budget template in the call)
org.who: Civil society organisations registered and operating in Türkiye (national or local). Organisations in the pilot provinces Afyon, Bilecik, Bitlis, Burdur, Tokat and Yalova are encouraged.
req: Awareness-raising and practical support for women in vulnerable situations seeking access to justice
Cooperation with the relevant bar association(s) is required
Application by email to the CoE Ankara office
org.how: Email the application package to the Council of Europe Programme Office in Ankara before the deadline.
org.tip: Bilecik is a pilot province in IDDA's TR41 region; a digital legal-literacy tool for women, built with a local bar association, would fit.

org.title: Czech Embassy Ankara: Transition Promotion Programme (TRANS) 2027
org.funder: Embassy of the Czech Republic in Ankara
org.who: Local non-governmental organisations in Türkiye, including local branches of international NGOs.
req: Priorities: civil society & human rights defenders; freedom of expression & media; political and public participation; rule of law; equality & non-discrimination; human rights in labour and environmental protection
Identification Form (XLSX) in English, signed (and stamped)
Proof of legal registration and of the signatory's authority
org.period: Up to 8 months, between 1 March and 31 October 2027
org.how: Email the form and documents to ankara@mzv.gov.cz. Funding depends on the Czech state budget allocation.
org.tip: A youth civic-participation or environmental-rights project with a digital component matches several priorities.

org.title: Netherlands Embassy: Human Rights Fund & MATRA (Societal Transformation)
org.funder: Embassy of the Netherlands in Ankara & Consulate-General in Istanbul
org.dlText: The embassy plans to reopen the call at the end of this year
org.amount: Varies by call
org.who: Organisations promoting human rights and the rule of law in Türkiye.
req: Dutch priorities: freedom of expression, internet freedom and independent journalism; freedom of religion and belief; equal rights for women and girls; protection of human rights defenders
Read the Human Rights Fund and MATRA application guidelines before applying
org.how: Watch the embassy page for the new call and guidelines.
org.tip: Prepare a concept now so you can submit as soon as the call opens.

org.title: Canada Fund for Local Initiatives (CFLI) – Türkiye
org.dlText: Annual call; the 2026 call closed on 30 March 2026, so the next is expected in spring 2027
org.who: Local NGOs, community and non-profit organisations, local academic institutions, and international NGOs working locally.
req: Thematic priorities: inclusive governance; peace and security; growth that works for everyone
Proposal in English with a gender-based analysis
Two-step selection (concept note first)
org.how: Apply via the CFLI Türkiye page when the call opens.
org.tip: Small, high-impact local projects; e.g. digital skills for young women in Eskişehir.

org.title: GEF Small Grants Programme Türkiye
org.dlText: Project calls are published periodically (a 2026 call was announced)
org.amount: Up to USD 50,000 per project
org.who: Local and national associations and foundations working on environment, development, women or youth; women's, agricultural and forest cooperatives.
req: Biodiversity conservation, climate change mitigation/adaptation, or preventing land degradation
Community-based approach with tangible environmental benefits
org.how: Follow GEF SGP Türkiye announcements (also shared by STGM).
org.tip: Perfect for a community solar or circular-economy pilot linked to IDDA's climate education work.

org.title: POLICY ENLARGE: small grants for cross-border R&I cooperation (Horizon Europe)
org.funder: Horizon Europe project (TÜBİTAK is a partner)
org.amount: Up to €8,000 per project (80% funding); mobility grants up to €5,000
org.who: Non-profit entities, companies, research organisations and academic groups in enlargement countries: Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Kosovo, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia, Türkiye and Ukraine.
req: At least 2 independent organisations from 2 different enlargement countries (a Türkiye-based NGO needs a partner from another enlargement country)
Joint regional innovation actions or uptake of research results; up to 6 months
20% co-funding; lump-sum payment against results
org.how: Apply in English via the OnePass platform (opportunities.getonepass.eu/opportunities/policy-enlarge).
org.tip: A quick, small grant to start a digital-education or AI-literacy pilot with a partner in Serbia or Ukraine.

org.title: Digital Democracy Initiative & CIVICUS Crisis Response Fund: Digital Resiliency Grants
org.funder: CIVICUS · co-funded by Denmark and the EU
org.amount: Up to USD 10,000 (rapid response)
org.who: Civil society actors facing urgent digital or civic-space threats, in countries whose civic space is rated 'obstructed' or 'repressed' by the CIVICUS Monitor.
req: Must respond to an imminent civic-space threat or emergency (not regular project funding)
Use of digital technology to counter threats and continue work
org.how: Apply via the CIVICUS Digital Resiliency Grants page.
org.tip: Only relevant if IDDA or a partner faces an urgent digital threat; keep it in mind for emergencies.

org.title: German–Turkish Youth Bridge (Deutsch-Türkische Jugendbrücke)
org.dlText: Several programmes with their own deadlines; small project fund (KPF) for flexible co-financing
org.amount: Funding for German–Turkish youth & school exchanges; small-project co-financing
org.who: German organisations and schools together with a partner organisation in Türkiye (applications are usually submitted by the German partner).
req: German–Turkish youth encounters, school exchanges and city-based youth projects
Inclusion and diversity principles; child-protection code of conduct signed by the Turkish partner
org.how: Find a German partner and check the current calls on jugendbruecke.de.
org.tip: Pair with IDDA's German contacts (e.g. TUM network) for a youth exchange on climate or digital topics.

org.title: Sabancı Foundation Open Call Grant Program
org.dlText: 2026 concept-note window was 9–27 February 2026; watch for the next open call
org.amount: 7 – 10 million TL per project for 3 years
org.who: Civil society organisations in Türkiye (no partnership required).
req: Trust-based, long-term support aligned with the foundation's themes (2026: quality and inclusive education)
Concept note first, via Submittable
org.how: Follow sabancivakfi.org for the next open call.
org.tip: Large, long-term education grant; worth preparing an evidence-based programme proposal.

org.title: European Youth Foundation (Council of Europe)
org.amount: One-off international activities up to €25,000; long-term projects up to €60,000
org.who: Youth NGOs and networks in Council of Europe member states (incl. Türkiye and Estonia), registered and validated in the EYF online system.
req: Promote human rights, democracy, intercultural understanding and youth participation
International activities involve participants from several Council of Europe member states
Register your NGO in the EYF system well before the deadline
org.period: Regular deadlines every year: 1 April and 1 October
org.how: Register and apply via the EYF online system (support4youth.coe.int).
org.tip: Strong fit for an international youth training on digital citizenship or climate democracy.

org.title: Nordplus 2027 (Adult, Horizontal, Junior, Higher Education)
org.amount: Project, network and mobility grants (5 cost categories)
org.who: Institutions and organisations working in education and lifelong learning in the Nordic and Baltic countries (incl. Estonia).
req: Cooperation projects usually need partners from at least 3 Nordplus countries
Nordplus Adult: organisations in adult education, VET or non-formal education
Nordplus Horizontal: partners from at least 2 different sectors
org.how: Apply via the Nordplus online application system.
org.tip: IDDA Estonia could lead a non-formal education network on digital or climate skills with Nordic partners.

org.title: KIK Environmental Programme (environmental awareness & co-financing)
org.dlText: Several programme lines are 'in preparation'; watch KIK for new rounds
org.amount: Varies by programme
org.who: Estonian organisations including NGOs (MTÜs), local authorities and companies.
req: Environmental awareness programme (environmental education)
Co-financing programme for projects funded by LIFE, Interreg, etc.
Raising pupils' awareness of green technologies (in preparation)
org.how: Follow kik.ee for open rounds.
org.tip: Use co-financing to cover the own contribution of an IDDA Estonia LIFE or Interreg project.

org.title: CSO Grant to promote democracy and CSO engagement with the Council of Europe
org.funder: Council of Europe · Civil Society Unit
org.amount: Up to €20,000 per grant (3–4 grants; at least 5% co-financing)
org.who: Legally constituted NGOs in a Council of Europe member state with at least five years of advocacy or policy work on democracy, civic space, rule of law or human rights.
req: Project must involve participants from at least four Council of Europe member states
Only one application per organisation; INGOs and consortia are preferred
Annual report, audited accounts and proof of legal status required
org.how: Email the signed application form, budget and annexes to NGO-Unit@coe.int with the subject 'Application for CSO Grant'.
org.tip: IDDA could lead a four-country consortium (e.g. Türkiye, Estonia, Italy, Romania) on youth civic participation and the Reykjavik Principles.

org.title: National Endowment for Democracy (NED) grants
org.amount: No fixed ceiling: budget should match the activities
org.who: Independent non-governmental organisations outside the United States working on democracy, human rights, independent media or civic participation (100+ countries).
req: Online application through NED's portal (several languages available)
Three decision rounds a year; late proposals move to the next round
Strong context analysis and track record expected
org.how: Read the regional priorities on ned.org, then apply via the online portal.
org.tip: Best for civic-education or youth-participation projects with a clear democracy angle.

org.title: European Endowment for Democracy (EED) – rolling support
org.dlText: Requests are accepted all year round
org.amount: Requests usually range from €10,000 to €150,000 (no formal range)
org.who: Civil society organisations, movements, independent media, youth groups and activists in the European Neighbourhood, the Western Balkans and Türkiye; formal registration is not required.
req: Pro-democracy focus: civic participation, independent media, human rights, youth activism
Applications accepted in several languages, including Turkish
org.how: Submit a request through the EED support page.
org.tip: Flexible, fast funding for youth civic initiatives that other donors find too small or too new.

org.title: UN Democracy Fund (UNDEF)
org.dlText: Proposals are accepted only during an annual online window (the last announced window was 1–28 February 2025)
org.amount: Project grants (two-year projects)
org.who: Civil society organisations working on democracy, human rights and participation, mainly in developing and transitional countries.
req: Online submission only, in English or French
Very competitive: usually one funded proposal per organisation
org.how: Watch un.org/democracyfund for the next call window.
org.tip: Prepare a two-year concept on youth participation in local decision-making so you can submit as soon as the window opens.

org.title: Wikimedia Rapid Fund
org.dlText: Several rounds a year; check the Rapid Fund cycle timeline
org.who: Individuals, groups and organisations anywhere working on Wikimedia-related projects (e.g. Wikipedia editathons, open knowledge, digital literacy).
req: Short projects of 1–12 months with a Wikimedia focus
No travel scholarships; research projects go to the Research Fund
org.how: Apply via the Wikimedia Foundation grantee portal (Fluxx).
org.tip: A Wikipedia editathon on climate or women in science with IDDA volunteers is an easy, fundable first project.

org.title: European Climate Initiative (EUKI) – call for project ideas
org.dlText: One call for project ideas per year (two-step: short outline, then full proposal)
org.who: NGOs, local authorities, non-profit enterprises and education institutions in EU member states and Western Balkan candidate countries.
req: Cross-border climate action with partners in several European countries
At least half of the funds must go to target countries
org.how: Sign up for the 'remind me' alert on euki.de and submit an outline when the call opens.
org.tip: IDDA Estonia could lead a Baltic–Balkan climate-education project.

org.title: Japan's Grant Assistance for Grassroots Human Security Projects (GGP)
org.dlText: Each Japanese embassy publishes its own call and deadlines
org.amount: Usually up to around JPY 10–25 million, depending on the embassy
org.who: Non-profit organisations, local authorities, schools and hospitals in countries where the Japanese embassy runs GGP (140+ countries and regions).
req: Grassroots projects meeting basic human needs (health, education, water, livelihoods)
Often focused on equipment or small infrastructure
org.how: Check the website of the Japanese embassy in your country for its GGP page.
org.tip: Equipment for a community digital-skills lab is a typical GGP-style request.

org.title: U.S. Embassy Public Diplomacy small grants
org.dlText: Each U.S. embassy publishes its own notices of funding opportunity during the year
org.amount: Often USD 5,000 – 75,000 (e.g. USD 15,000–50,000 in Türkiye's 2025 call)
org.who: Non-profits, educational institutions and individuals in the host country, depending on each embassy's notice.
req: Projects must match the embassy's published themes
Registration on grants.gov / SAM.gov is usually required
org.how: Search simpler.grants.gov for your country's U.S. embassy or check the embassy website.
org.tip: English-language, STEM or entrepreneurship programmes for young people often match the themes.

org.title: Canada Fund for Local Initiatives (CFLI)
org.dlText: Each Canadian embassy runs an annual call, often in spring
org.amount: Typically CAD 20,000 – 100,000, depending on the country
org.who: Local NGOs, community organisations and other local actors in CFLI-eligible countries.
req: Small, local projects in Canada's priority areas (e.g. inclusive governance, gender equality, climate)
Gender-based analysis usually required
org.how: Find your country's CFLI page on international.gc.ca.
org.tip: Keep a short concept ready; calls are often open for only a few weeks.

org.title: GEF Small Grants Programme (SGP)
org.dlText: Each SGP country programme publishes its own calls
org.amount: Usually up to USD 50,000 per project
org.who: NGOs and community-based organisations in countries with an SGP country programme.
req: Biodiversity, climate change, land degradation, chemicals or international waters
Community-based approach
org.how: Find your SGP national coordinator on sgp.undp.org.
org.tip: Pair environmental action with youth education for a stronger proposal.

org.title: Ministry of Interior: Project Support for Associations (STİGM)
org.funder: İçişleri Bakanlığı Sivil Toplumla İlişkiler Genel Müdürlüğü
org.dlText: In 2026, about 400 associations received a total of 350 million TL between 10 February and 20 September; the next window is expected early in 2027
org.amount: Project support for associations (amount depends on the project)
org.who: Associations (dernekler) registered in Türkiye.
req: Priority areas include family, women's rights and prevention of violence, NGO capacity, public–civil society cooperation, social entrepreneurship and disaster preparedness
Some project types require documented cooperation with a public body (e.g. district governorate or education directorate)
org.how: Follow the STİGM website and DERBİS announcements; apply online with the yearly application guide.
org.tip: A capacity-building project on digital skills for NGO volunteers fits the 'institutional capacity' priority.

org.title: SOGEP – Social Development Support Programme (via BEBKA)
org.funder: Ministry of Industry and Technology · Development Agencies
org.dlText: Development agencies usually collect project ideas in spring; projects are developed together with the agency (guided-project method)
org.amount: Project-based (guided projects; large budgets)
org.who: Public institutions, municipalities and NGOs in the region; in the TR41 region (Bursa, Eskişehir, Bilecik) it is run by BEBKA.
req: Two-stage process: project proposal form, then joint development with the agency
Focus on disadvantaged groups, youth employment and social inclusion
org.how: Send a project proposal form to BEBKA during the SOGEP pre-application period.
org.tip: Team up with Eskişehir municipality or a public body on a youth employability and digital-skills programme.

org.title: Cultural Endowment of Estonia (Kultuurkapital)
org.dlText: Applications can be submitted in four rounds a year
org.amount: Grants for cultural projects, events and travel
org.who: Individuals and organisations (including NGOs) working in culture, arts, sport and folk culture in Estonia.
req: Apply to the relevant field endowment (e.g. folk culture, sport, literature)
Activities must take place within the grant period
org.how: Apply through the kulka.ee e-environment during an open round.
org.tip: Use it for the cultural part of a youth event (performances, creative workshops).

org.title: ESTDEV: Global education & awareness-raising projects in Estonia
org.dlText: Annual call for global-education projects in Estonia; ESTDEV also runs country calls (e.g. Ukraine, Moldova, Armenia)
org.amount: Project grants (2026: seven projects shared about €366,000)
org.who: Estonian NGOs and other organisations working on global education and development awareness.
req: Projects raising awareness of global development, sustainability and humanitarian issues
Usually 5% own contribution in ESTDEV calls
org.how: Follow estdev.ee for the next call.
org.tip: A youth global-citizenship programme linking Estonian and Turkish schools fits well.

org.title: Integration Foundation (Integratsiooni Sihtasutus) calls
org.dlText: Several calls a year (e.g. national-minority culture, integration activities, Estonian communities abroad)
org.amount: Varies by call
org.who: Estonian NGOs, cultural societies and community organisations.
req: Projects supporting integration, Estonian language and culture, or national minority cultures
org.how: Check integratsioon.ee for open calls.
org.tip: Ideal for inclusive youth activities that mix Estonian- and Russian-speaking young people.

youth.title: Türkiye Scholarships 2027 (Türkiye Bursları)
youth.dlNote: Expected dates based on the yearly calendar
youth.get: Full tuition, monthly stipend, accommodation, health insurance, flight ticket and a one-year Turkish course
youth.who: International students (non-Turkish citizens): bachelor's under 21, master's under 30, PhD under 35

youth.title: Stipendium Hungaricum 2027/28
youth.dlNote: Expected deadline based on the previous cycle
youth.get: Tuition-free studies in Hungary with a monthly stipend and housing support
youth.who: Students from around 80 partner countries; you also need a nomination from your country's sending partner

el.n: Only for nationals of Stipendium Hungaricum partner countries (Türkiye is one); check the list

youth.title: Swedish Institute Scholarship for Global Professionals 2027/28
youth.dlNote: Apply to an eligible master's programme by 15 January 2027 first, then for the scholarship on 8–24 February 2027
youth.get: Full tuition, SEK 12,000 per month and a travel grant
youth.who: Professionals with leadership experience from 34 eligible countries

el.n: Only for citizens of the listed eligible countries, with work and leadership experience

youth.title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters 2027
youth.dlText: Each programme sets its own deadline; most close between December 2026 and January 2027
youth.get: Full scholarships for top-ranked students: participation costs, travel and monthly living allowance; 37 new programmes for 2027
youth.who: Bachelor's graduates from any country

youth.title: One Young World: Generation Regen Challenge
youth.get: Fully funded place at the One Young World Summit 2027 in Tokyo (28 Sept – 1 Oct): flights, accommodation and catering
youth.who: Young leaders (18+) working on regenerative, climate and nature solutions

youth.title: Hult Prize 2027
youth.dlText: Campus and global qualifiers run through early 2027; check your university's date
youth.get: US$1,000,000 seed funding for the winning team, plus mentorship and incubation
youth.who: Teams of 2–4 university students, all aged 18+ by 28 February 2027, building a for-profit startup that advances a UN SDG

youth.title: Y Combinator: next batch
youth.dlText: Winter 2027 deadline was 2 November 2026; late applications are still read, and new batches run quarterly
youth.get: US$500,000 investment and a 3-month programme in San Francisco
youth.who: Startup founders worldwide, from idea stage up

youth.title: EIT Jumpstarter 2027
youth.dlText: Next call expected spring 2027 (2026 closed in May)
youth.get: 7-month pre-acceleration: training, mentors, investor access and up to €10,000 in prizes; no equity
